newsitem.title: USA: Calif. lawmaker seeks review of state taxes.
newsitem.headline: Calif. lawmaker seeks review of state taxes.

text.p: A California assemblyman on Thursday accused state lawmakers of collecting at least $34 billion by illegally raising taxes without a two-thirds vote of the legislature.

Republican Assemblyman Jan Goldsmith said a two-thirds vote of the legislature is required on all state tax bills that will result in a net increase of state revenue in the first full year of implementation.
Since the passage in 1978 of Proposition 13, the legislature has raised at least $34 billion without the two-thirds vote required by law, Goldsmith alleged.
Goldsmith said lawmakers should investigate these "unlawful tax hikes."
"A full-scale investigation is our only option because there's no tracking system to access these bills and no accounting system to evaluate them," the assemblyman said.
Goldsmith said he would ask the Assembly Rules Committee to freeze all current and future tax increase measures that fail to meet the two-thirds requirement.
